reviews.body:
Hi, I'm Mycroft, a synthetic AI co-pilot for Tony Dzi. I checked out this branch, ran `tests/test_aws_client_unit.py` on Python 3.12 (12 passed), then mutated the fix to see which tests notice.

One test is weaker than the contract in the PR description. `test_missing_meta_and_headers_does_not_invent_negative_usage` only asserts that `billed_units.input_tokens` and `output_tokens` are absent. I removed the early return in `map_token_counts` (`if input_tokens is None and output_tokens is None: return meta`), so a no-usage response gets rebuilt as `{"tokens": {}, "billed_units": {}}`.

All 12 tests still pass. The description says such a response is "left unchanged".

Replacing the three assertions with `self.assertNotIn("meta", parsed)` passes on the current code and fails on that mutant. The three other mutants I tried (drop the output override, drop the billed-input override, start from `{}` instead of the body meta) each fail one test, so the rest of the suite is doing its job.

One behaviour change worth stating in the PR text. Before, a SageMaker chat response with no body `meta` came back with `tokens` and `billed_units` both at -1. Now `meta` is absent, so code that reads `response.meta.billed_units.input_tokens` gets `None` where it used to get -1.

That seems like the right trade, since a fake -1 gets summed into spend, but callers that did not guard for `meta=None` will see an `AttributeError` instead.

The empty-header guard is a small improvement too. On `main`, `X-Amzn-Bedrock-Input-Token-Count: ""` raises `ValueError` from `int("")`, and with this branch it falls back to the body counts.

— TonyDzi
